newsitem.title: USA: UAW issues strike deadline to GM supplier.
newsitem.headline: UAW issues strike deadline to GM supplier.

text.p: In another strike threat to an auto parts maker, the United Auto Workers union on Thursday it issued a Friday night strike deadline against American Axle & Manufacturing Inc, the main supplier of truck axles to General Motors Corp.

UAW spokesman Reg McGhee said about 7,500 workers in Detroit, Three Rivers, Mich., and Buffalo, N.Y., would go on strike on Friday at 1159 EST (0459 GMT) if company and union negotiators failed to reach an agreement on a new contract.

The contract negotiations between American Axle and the UAW are significant because they are the first since the company bought several plants from GM in February 1994. The company was formed by former Chrysler Corp manufacturing chief Richard Dauch.

Previously, American Axle's workers were covered under the same terms of GM's 1993 national UAW contract. The current negotiations could affect GM's ability to sell other plants to independent companies, according to industry analysts.

A prolonged strike at American Axle also could virtually paralyze production of GM light trucks, since the company supplies almost all of the automaker's rear-drive truck axles and brake housings. The company also produces some products for Chrysler trucks.

Union officials said American Axle was unwilling to meet all of the terms of the 1996 GM agreement, which calls for the automaker to guarantee jobs for 95 percent of its current workforce, make a $2,000 lump-sum payment in the first year and provide three percent raises in the second and third years.

A particular area of disagreement is the "grow-in" rate for new employees. Under the GM pact, new hires reach full wage rates after three years on the job, but officials said American Axle wanted to extend that period in order to stay competitive with other suppliers.
A spokesman for American Axle was not immediately available for comment.
